research_question: Among adults with early-stage oral cavity (including oral tongue) squamous cell carcinoma and a clinically node-negative neck, what is the effect of elective immediate prophylactic neck dissection, compared with therapeutic delayed neck dissection after watchful waiting until nodal relapse, on disease-free survival?
treatment_label: Elective (immediate, prophylactic) neck dissection performed at the time of primary tumour surgery
control_label: Therapeutic (delayed) neck dissection after watchful waiting, performed only if nodal disease appears
outcome_description: Disease-free survival, including synonymous event-free, relapse-free, or recurrence-free survival, defined as time to new disease, recurrence, disease progression, or death from any cause. Extract the hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval for elective versus therapeutic neck dissection, preferring intention-to-treat estimates and the longest available follow-up. Do not substitute overall survival/death-only hazard ratios or pool locoregional recurrence, recurrence proportions, adverse events, or quality of life.
positive_direction: For standardized coding, a positive effect means longer disease-free survival and therefore a result favoring elective neck dissection; for the requested hazard-ratio analysis specifically, HR below 1 favors elective neck dissection.
search_queries: oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma elective therapeutic neck dissection randomized trial disease-free survival
oral tongue cancer prophylactic neck dissection watchful waiting controlled trial event-free survival
clinically node-negative oral cancer immediate delayed neck dissection randomized recurrence-free survival
inclusion_criteria: Original randomized controlled trials enrolling adults with early-stage oral cavity, including oral tongue, squamous cell carcinoma and a clinically node-negative neck, comparing elective with therapeutic neck dissection.
Treatment arms correspond to elective neck dissection at primary tumour surgery versus observation with neck dissection only after clinically apparent nodal relapse.

Reports disease-free, event-free, relapse-free, or recurrence-free survival and provides a hazard ratio with uncertainty, or sufficient log-rank information to derive a hazard ratio and variance using accepted indirect methods.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, protocols without results, and narrative reviews.

No comparison between an elective neck-dissection treatment condition and a therapeutic/watchful-waiting control condition; also exclude single-arm studies, non-randomized comparisons, and trials evaluating radiotherapy or sentinel-node biopsy only.

No quantitative disease-free-survival data capable of producing the requested effect size: no HR with 95% CI and no usable log-rank observed-minus-expected information, variance, or arm-level event counts together with a log-rank p-value; means and SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios alone are not adequate for this time-to-event outcome.

Completely unrelated to early-stage oral cavity/oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma with a clinically node-negative neck, or reports only overall survival/death, locoregional recurrence, recurrence rates, adverse events, or quality of life without eligible disease-free-survival information.
moderators_to_extract: Oral cavity subsite, including oral tongue versus other oral cavity sites
Tumour stage and T-stage eligibility distribution
Extent and type of elective neck dissection
HR source and analysis method: directly reported versus Peto O-E/V versus Parmar indirect estimation, and intention-to-treat versus other analysis
effect_size_note: Pool hazard ratios using a random-effects model on log(HR), with 95% confidence intervals. Orient every estimate as elective versus therapeutic neck dissection; if reported in the reverse direction, use HR_new=1/HR_original and swap/invert the confidence limits. HR<1 indicates lower event hazard and longer disease-free survival with elective dissection. Prefer the paper's intention-to-treat HR and the longest follow-up. Convert a reported 95% CI to SE[log(HR)] as (ln upper CI - ln lower CI)/(2*1.96). If no DFS HR is reported, derive log(HR) and its variance only from adequate log-rank information using standard indirect methods: Peto O-E/V when observed-minus-expected and variance are available, or Parmar methods when arm-level events plus a log-rank p-value are available; record the method used. Exclude a study from this outcome if neither a DFS HR nor sufficient log-rank statistics are available. Do not use an overall-survival or death-only HR as a proxy.
